title: Duplexer Module - n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Olaf Bergstrom

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Duplexer Module filter targeting n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter. The filter is designed on AlN on SiC substrate with a target center frequency of 4010.3 MHz and bandwidth of 313.1 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Duplexer Module
- Frequency Band: n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR)
- Application: GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
- Substrate: AlN on SiC
- Package: WLP (Wafer Level Package)
- Design Tool: Cadence AWR Microwave Office
- Design Center: San Jose Advanced Design Lab

This specification applies to all variants of the Duplexer Module design targeting n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       4010.3 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       313.1 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 2.5 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 20.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 36.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 40.0 dB
Q Factor:               12683
Temperature Coefficient:-17.1 ppm/°C
Die Size:               0.9 x 0.5 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   9
Electrode Material:     Mo
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Cadence AWR Microwave Office and load the Duplexer Module template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on SiC with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 4010.3 MHz, BW 313.1 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 2.5 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (WLP (Wafer Level Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, AlN on SiC).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz FSW Signal Analyzer.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 12031 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 2.5 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 20.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 470 MHz offset >= 36.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 9 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 8.6 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +29 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 1000 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 87%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-08-27
Devices Tested:         32
Insertion Loss (meas):  2.18 dB
Return Loss (meas):     21.6 dB
Rejection (meas):       39.0 dB
Isolation (meas):       45.3 dB
Q Factor (meas):        12683
Group Delay Variation:  4.4 ns
Power Handling:         +33 dBm
Die Yield:              85.0%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Duplexer Module design demonstrated acceptable performance for n79 (4.4-5.0 GHz 5G NR).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Wafer-level uniformity was excellent (sigma < 1.5%).
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
